analysis.title: GS Wijaya - GS SECTOR SPECIALISTS Energy, Natural Resources and Utilities Preview 2 Stocks 6 Nov 2026
key_insights: DVN is expected to be the most in-focus O&G stock of the day. The desk had positioning at 5/10 going into the print, and investor requests for positioning views ahead of the print were extremely elevated.
DVN inbounds after yesterday's close were negative. GS sees potential for more pressure on DVN today relative to the rest of the group.
DVN quarter: EPS ahead, oil volumes slightly below, cash flow ahead. 4Q oil production guidance at the midpoint is slightly below the Street (555 Mbo/d vs Street 559 Mbo/d).
DVN 2026 guidance was maintained on total production and capital spend. 2027 guidance looks generally in line on MBOE/d, with an annual oil production growth rate of 1-3% over a multi-year period.

DVN shareholder letter focuses on the go-forward portfolio. After the Eagle Ford sale, the company calls Anadarko, Marcellus and Rockies complementary assets providing 'significant optionality between O&G targets', with the Permian as the cornerstone.
DVN bull case: 16% FCF yield on 2027 GS numbers, a ramping buyback, clarity after the strategic review, and the stock having already lagged Large Cap peers.

DVN bear case: the stock has historically traded at a discount, talk of ground game and growth is not necessarily what the market wanted (asset sales were the main catalyst), a buyback with WTI at $90/b raises questions, and DVN must compete for capital with E&P peers COP (best FCF inflection incoming), OXY (leverage reduction) and OVV (similar-ish valuation, well-received ground game).
DK is described as one of the better Refining and SMID prints this quarter. The open question is how much the micro matters given the market's focus on the macro (cracks).
DK 3Q adj EPS was $10.53 vs Street $8.05. A $50 mn buyback is ahead of the GS model for 3Q, and the company plans to buy back $100 mn of stock in 4Q, which is new for DK.
DKL raised FY26 non-refining adj EBITDA guidance, seen as a small win. Early feedback on DK is generally more positive.

market_movers.rationale: GS sees potential for more pressure on DVN than the rest of the group after negative post-close inbounds, despite an EPS beat. Bulls cite a 16% FCF yield on 2027 GS numbers, bears cite a buyback with WTI at $90/b.
3Q adj EPS of $10.53 vs Street $8.05, a new $100 mn 4Q buyback plan, and a raised DKL FY26 non-refining adj EBITDA guide. Early feedback is generally positive.

sector_views.rationale: DVN is expected to lag the group on the print, while peers COP, OXY and OVV are named as competing for capital on FCF inflection, leverage reduction and valuation.
DK's print is called one of the better Refining and SMID prints this quarter, though the macro focus on cracks may outweigh the company-specific results.

earnings_insights: DVN 3Q (reported 11/5 after close): EPS ahead of expectations for the quarter, oil volumes slightly below, cash flow ahead. The report gives no EPS figures.
DVN 4Q oil production guidance midpoint is 555 Mbo/d vs Street estimate 559 Mbo/d.
DVN 2026 guidance maintained on total production and capital spend. 2027 guidance generally in line on MBOE/d, with annual oil production growth of 1-3% over a multi-year period.
DVN trades at a 16% FCF yield on 2027 GS estimates (GS model figure, not a reported number).
DK 3Q adj EPS reported $10.53 vs Street estimate $8.05.
DK 3Q buyback of $50 mn is ahead of the GS model. DK plans $100 mn of buybacks in 4Q.
DKL raised FY26 non-refining adj EBITDA guidance. No figure is given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Cited by bears as a reason to question DVN leaning into a buyback at this oil price.

risk_factors: DVN has historically traded at a discount to peers.
The market may not welcome DVN's emphasis on growth and the ground game, as asset sales were the main catalyst.
DVN buyback at WTI $90/b raises questions, and DVN competes for capital with other E&Ps.
Refiner macro (crack spreads) may outweigh micro results such as DK's beat.
